A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Supervised Guidance Training work. The main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching material across table renumbering and figure relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on sparse observations, heat-equation inversion, and MNIST shape inpainting in Section 5, Tables 1–3, and Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds smaller conditional-diffusion comparisons, imperfect-score experiments, and an original resolution-generalization study.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1, the SGT objective in Equation 23, the guidance parameterization in Equation 25, and covariance preconditioning are unchanged. The additional model configurations serve experimental comparisons without revising SGT.

E1.justification: The sinusoidal data, heat-equation task, and MNIST digit-3 shapes are retained. Appendix C.4 adds an unconditional generation scenario testing transfer from 32-point training to 64- and 128-point sampling on the existing sinusoidal distribution.

E2.justification: Appendix C.4 introduces an evaluated finite-dimensional 1D U-Net comparator against the infinite-dimensional neural-operator model. The original FunDPS and conditional-diffusion comparators remain.

E3.justification: Section 5.2 adds conditional diffusion approximately matched to the guidance network's parameter count and training steps; an SGT-size variant also appears in the heat-equation table. New studies compare random, 50-epoch, and fully trained base models, and train at 32 points before sampling at 32, 64, and 128 points. These are focused additions to the retained benchmark protocols.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained preconditioner comparisons, v2 adds two substantive robustness investigations: sensitivity to unconditional-score quality in Section 5.2, Table 2, and Figure 8, and generalization beyond training resolution in Appendix C.4 and Figure 7. These substantially expand the diagnostic evidence concerning practical score errors and the claimed resolution advantage.

E5.justification: Existing mean-plus-standard-deviation summaries and posterior spread displays remain. No new repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, or significance-testing procedures are introduced. Figure 8 further displays posterior standard deviation using the existing uncertainty concept.

E6.justification: Original benchmark values are retained apart from equivalent rounding. Added SGT-size conditional-diffusion rows report RMSE 0.406 for sparse observations and 0.0483 for heat inversion. New Table 2 reports, for example, RMSE 0.397 for SGT versus 0.472 for FunDPS with the partly trained base model. Figures 7–8 add qualitative resolution-transfer and random-base-model findings.

T1.justification: The assumptions, Theorems 3.1–3.2, Propositions 4.1–4.2, and mathematical arguments in Appendices A–B are unchanged. Appendix A is identical; the edits in Appendix B are grammatical.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statement, and conclusion retain the same claims about infinite-dimensional conditioning, conditional-score decomposition, simulation-free SGT, and improved accuracy over heuristic guidance. The added experiments support these claims without redefining the principal contribution.

C2.justification: v2 explains how learned guidance can partly compensate for an imperfect base score and clarifies that SGT inference uses both unconditional and guidance networks. Appendix C.4 distinguishes accepting higher-resolution inputs from meaningful resolution generalization. The conclusion retains the limitation concerning unconditional-score approximation errors.

D1.justification: v2 supplies limited implementation information for the new studies, including the 1D U-Net comparator, 32-point training discretization, 50-epoch partial training, and FunDPS guidance scales in Table 2. The original detailed implementation descriptions and code-access disclosure remain unchanged; the new configurations are not documented as fully.

R1.justification: v2 adds Pieper-Sethmacher and Paulin (2026) and Pieper-Sethmacher et al. (2025) to the diffusion and h-transform background. Appendix C.4 also connects its resolution experiment to the already-cited Hagemann et al. (2025). The broader positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: Changes comprise targeted expansions in Section 5.2, the new Appendix C.4, an introductory cross-reference, and small grammar and notation corrections. Author affiliation, acknowledgments, and conference information are updated. The overall narrative and section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds Table 2 and Figures 7–8, expands the sparse-observation and heat-equation tables with smaller-model rows, and relocates Figures 2–3. The heat and shape tables are renumbered, and Figure 4's h-Transform label becomes Supervised Guidance Training. Existing graphics and the general layout are otherwise retained.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens the empirical support through a comparison matched to guidance-training resources, imperfect-score tests, and resolution-transfer examples. Its clarification of SGT's combined inference cost also improves interpretation of the efficiency comparison. These are useful but limited gains: the added studies remain narrow, some configuration details are sparse, and the underlying method and theory are unchanged.
